messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** the freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C** (about –1.9 °C to –2.1 °C depending on the source).  

This is because the solid‑liquid coexistence line for water has a negative slope: as the pressure falls below atmospheric, ice melts at a lower temperature. At 10 kPa (≈0.1 atm) the equilibrium temperature between ice and liquid water is about two degrees below zero.
